chapter: Harlem, the Cotton Club and Duke Ellington
title: Never reading music; how he knew his cues in the orchestra
summary: He never read notes and learned his place at rehearsal; Duke would look at him when it was his turn to fill in.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I see. And at that point -- you never have read music at all, right?
I wouldn't know what a note looked like. I know what they look like, but you know, I wouldn't --
When you played with the orchestra then, how did you know when to come in? Did Duke just point at you?
Did Duke just point at you and say --
During the rehearsal I knew where to come in.
Uh-huh. And you'd go through -- they would rehearse and he would say, 'Well, there's a spot here and --
After the trumpet solo, or whatever.
He'd look at me and that meant that that was my turn.
To come in there and fill in whatever it was, see.
